newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Dozens believed trapped in Australia ski landslide.
newsitem.headline: Dozens believed trapped in Australia ski landslide.

text.p: Dozens of people are believed to have been trapped by a landslide on Wednesday night which caused the collapse of at least two ski lodges at Thredbo, Australia's favourite ski resort, police said on Thursday.
One police spokesman said he believed there had been several deaths but others said that at this stage there were no confirmed deaths or injuries.
Thredbo, Australia's most popular ski resort, is located in the Snowy Mountains of New South Wales state about 300 km (190 miles) southwest of Sydney.
It is the height of the ski season when Thredbo is packed with thousands of visitors.
A New South Wales fire brigade official told Reuters there had been an explosion, three lodges had been affected in the landslide and an unknown number of people were trapped.
Early radio reports spoke of up to 100 people being trapped.
The Australian Associated Press news agency quoted a police spokesman as saying: "There are multiple injuries at this stage. We are hoping that a third building does not go down too."
A massive emergency operation was being mounted with emergency services from the region rushing to the scene, police said.
An ambulance spokesman said the weather was too bad for helicopters to be used.
